title: Physics — 10 notable papers from the 28 October 2026 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred evidence-weighted ordering, not a popularity list, and citation evidence is limited for the newest papers.

sections.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
sections.abstract: The authors measure the beta decay of neutron-rich potassium-54 and find a dominant transition to an excited, neutron-unbound state in calcium-54, with ab initio calculations supporting an essential contribution from two-body weak currents.
sections.claimed_result: The FRIB measurement identifies a dominant feed to a neutron-unbound state near 6.16 MeV in calcium-54; the authors report that its Gamow–Teller strength agrees with ab initio calculations when two-body currents are included, which they interpret as direct evidence for their role in neutron-rich beta decay.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; beta-delayed gamma-ray and neutron time-of-flight spectroscopy at FRIB, compared with ab initio and shell-model calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The parent potassium-54 ground-state spin is inferred rather than definitively established, and low statistics leave weaker decay branches ambiguous; the authors also note discrepancies in calculated excitation energies and low-energy strength.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment says accepted for publication in Nature Communications; calculated results are deposited in Zenodo record 22666940; the paper is cross-listed between nuclear experiment and theory.

sections.title: High significance measurement of reactor coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering on germanium by CONUS+
sections.abstract: Using CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at the Leibstadt reactor, the authors report 1,555 ± 152 reactor CEνNS events at 10.2σ and determine the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer near 10 MeV.
sections.claimed_result: For 1,296 kg·days of reactor-on exposure, the authors obtain 1,555 ± 152 CEνNS events, consistent with the Standard Model expectation of 1,701 ± 198; they also report sin²θW = 0.225 ± 0.022.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; reactor-antineutrino data from CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at Leibstadt, analyzed with a blind likelihood fit
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the result remains statistics-dominated; background modeling is their largest systematic on the signal, while near-threshold calibration and germanium quenching affect the predicted signal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports a blind-likelihood result with quantified event yield and significance, and is cross-listed in experimental and phenomenological high-energy physics. Its arXiv comment identifies a companion detailed-analysis paper submitted simultaneously.

sections.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of ϕ, K⁰S, and Λ elliptic flow
sections.abstract: ALICE reports the first elliptic-flow measurements for ϕ, K⁰S, and Λ hadrons in oxygen–oxygen collisions at √sNN = 5.36 TeV, finding low-momentum mass ordering and a significant intermediate-momentum baryon–meson split.
sections.claimed_result: In about three billion selected O–O collisions, the authors find a baryon–meson v₂ splitting above 3 GeV/c and a ϕ-meson pattern closer to the lighter K⁰S than to the similarly massive Λ; they argue this supports quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; identified-particle azimuthal correlations measured with the ALICE detector at the LHC
sections.unique_caveat: The collective-flow interpretation depends on suppressing residual non-flow correlations and on two-particle factorization; the authors present recombination as a supported interpretation, not a uniquely demonstrated mechanism.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New identified-hadron ALICE measurement, submitted to Physical Review Letters per arXiv comment, with an ALICE figure record; cross-listed in nuclear and high-energy experiment.

sections.title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
sections.abstract: The authors report tunable experimental signatures of electron–metal decoherence and quantitative agreement with a quantum-Brownian-motion model, proposing electron microchannels as a platform for further tests of quantum dissipation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say that electron–metal decoherence signatures can be continuously tuned in their electron-microchannel experiment, providing evidence for the Anglin–Paz–Zurek quantum-Brownian-motion proposal.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; electron microchannel system studying motional decoherence near a metal surface
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence concerns this particular electron–metal environment; the authors describe a future test of Caldeira–Leggett dissipation theory rather than claiming that the theory has now been fully tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete experimental claim with quantitative theory–experiment agreement, cross-listed in quantum physics, mesoscopic condensed matter, and atomic physics; no journal reference was listed in the metadata checked.

sections.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-Λ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
sections.abstract: ALICE presents the first antideuteron–net-Λ number-correlation measurement in Pb–Pb collisions and reports that it, together with a net-Λ cumulant, is described by the Thermal-FIST statistical hadronization model.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the antideuteron–net-Λ correlation and the normalized second-order net-Λ cumulant are both described by Thermal-FIST, interpreting this as evidence that antideuteron–antiproton correlations are driven by nucleosynthesis while correlations with non-nucleonic hadrons probe hadronization.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb–Pb collision measurements at the LHC, compared with the Thermal-FIST statistical hadronization model
sections.unique_caveat: The interpretation is model-dependent: agreement with Thermal-FIST supports, but does not by itself uniquely establish, the proposed separation between nucleosynthesis and hadronization effects.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First measurement, submitted to Physical Review Letters per the arXiv comment and linked to an ALICE publication/figure release; cross-listed in nuclear and high-energy experiment.

sections.title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
sections.abstract: Transmission-electron-microscope measurements and many-body modeling suggest transient Coulomb ordering in freely propagating electron pulses, with further stabilization regimes proposed theoretically.
sections.claimed_result: For photoemitted pulses containing up to nine electrons, the authors observe strong energy correlations at low particle number; they attribute transient ordering to a self-induced longitudinal potential and predict that weak transverse guiding could extend it to larger beams.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; transmission electron microscopy for pulses up to nine electrons, supported by many-body simulations and a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model
sections.unique_caveat: The measurement covers small pulsed populations; crystallization at larger particle number and periodic bunching in continuous beams are theoretical predictions, not observations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Combines number-resolved experimental energy correlations with simulations and a statistical-mechanical model; cross-listed between condensed matter and accelerator physics.

sections.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
sections.abstract: Using the GWTC-5.0 black-hole population posterior, the authors forecast a median of 6.6 LISA binary-black-hole detections above signal-to-noise ratio 8 in four years, with wider alternatives under different mass-population assumptions.
sections.claimed_result: The reference population gives 6.6⁺⁵·⁵₋₂·₂ expected detections in four years; one three-peak alternative raises the median to about 14 and produces a very broad upper tail, while roughly 39% of the reference detections could be multiband sources.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; population inference from the LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA GWTC-5.0 catalog and an O3 intermediate-mass-binary search, extrapolated to LISA and Cosmic Explorer
sections.unique_caveat: Forecasts depend on extrapolating high-mass population models; the authors caution that approximations may make the most extreme predicted counts unreliable.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Uses the released GWTC-5.0 population posterior and quantifies reference and alternative-model counts with credible intervals; cross-listed between astrophysics and gravitation.

sections.title: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that tracks magnetically labeled living cancer cells at subcellular resolution for up to 72 hours, including during division and migration.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say their widefield NV-magnetometry system follows magnetic signatures of labeled cancer cells through mitosis, remodeling, cluster formation, splitting, and migration, including dense regions where brightfield contrast fails.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry integrated with a live-cell incubator
sections.unique_caveat: The reported demonstration uses magnetically labeled cancer cells and a specialized incubator; performance for other cell types, labels, or label-free imaging is not established by the abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports single-cell tracking over multi-day runs and is cross-listed across optics, biophysics, and quantum physics; this is an instrument/platform result rather than a claim of new fundamental physics.

sections.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
sections.abstract: The authors propose sequentially adapted optical measurements that, in point-source and blind-estimation scenarios, reduce imaging error to within a factor of two to five of the quantum limit compared with direct imaging.
sections.claimed_result: The proposed Adaptive Information Mining framework dynamically reshapes measurement responses to maximize Fisher information; the authors report 2–5× closer estimation error to the quantum limit than direct imaging for point sources without prior knowledge of source positions or brightness.
sections.evidence_type: computational; theoretical quantum-information analysis and Monte Carlo evaluations of point-source, blind multi-parameter, and turbulence scenarios
sections.unique_caveat: The paper demonstrates a measurement-design framework in modeled scenarios; the abstract does not report an end-to-end telescope deployment or real-sky validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports a quantitative comparison to direct imaging and extends the approach to unknown source counts and turbulence-induced wavefront distortion; cross-listed in quantum physics and optics.

sections.title: Cosmological constraints on single-field inflation models from ACT/SPT data and observations at sub-Mpc scales
sections.abstract: The authors propose three classes of single-field inflation potentials that can enhance small-scale primordial perturbations while meeting ACT/SPT spectral-index bounds, though satisfying primordial-black-hole limits remains difficult.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that bump/dip-modified, step-like, and double-inflection-point potentials can raise small-scale curvature perturbations while keeping the scalar spectral index within the current 2σ range; some parameter choices can also match PTA observations.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; single-field inflation calculations constrained against ACT/SPT, CMB, BAO, PTA, PBH, and CMB-distortion observations
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on the selected potential families and datasets; the authors state that satisfying primordial-black-hole abundance constraints remains challenging.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Connects ACT/SPT constraints with BAO, pulsar-timing-array, primordial-black-hole, and CMB-distortion bounds; cross-listed across cosmology, gravitation, and high-energy theory.

sections.title: Physics — latest arXiv batch: 28 October 2026
sections.text: 10 notable recent papers, led by experiment-driven tests of neutrino and nuclear physics, small-system heavy-ion behavior, and quantum measurement methods. The report starts with direct measurements and then covers quantum sensing and astrophysical forecasts.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
items: Precision measurements as tests of theory: potassium-54 beta decay, reactor CEνNS, and ALICE O–O flow are separate systems, not independent confirmations.
Small-system heavy-ion physics: ALICE O–O flow and Pb–Pb antideuteron–Λ correlations probe different observables and collision systems.
Quantum-limited measurement and sensing: electron decoherence, adaptive super-resolution, and NV live-cell magnetic imaging use distinct platforms.
Observations feeding future reach: LISA forecasts from GWTC-5.0 and inflation constraints from ACT/SPT, PTA, and PBH datasets are complementary inference problems.
Correlations as a route to emergent order: few-electron energy correlations and ALICE multi-particle correlations concern different mechanisms.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
items: CONUS+ remains statistics-dominated, with background modeling, threshold calibration, and germanium quenching among the uncertainties; increase exposure and improve those calibrations.
Potassium-54 parent spin and weak branches remain uncertain, and calculations overpredict some excitation energies; collect more FRIB spectroscopy and refine multi-shell ab initio treatments.

The origin of small-system flow signatures remains unsettled and non-flow effects complicate interpretation; measure more species/observables and compare initial-state and hydrodynamic/recombination models.
LISA forecasts vary widely under high-mass population extrapolations; update population posteriors and compare a broader set of mass models.
Candidate inflation potentials still face PBH abundance limits; perform a joint analysis of CMB, PTA, PBH, and CMB-distortion constraints.

QCM has demonstrated magnetically labeled cancer-cell imaging and AIM has modeled-scene super-resolution; test across cell/label conditions and validate adaptive imaging in an optical setup with controlled turbulence.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The batch is strongest where new data directly confront a specific physical mechanism: reactor CEνNS, neutron-rich beta decay, and collective-flow signatures in light-ion collisions. Quantum sensing and imaging add promising methods, while LISA and inflation remain forecasts or model-dependent inferences.

sections.title: Method and sources
sections.text: Daily batch 2026-10-28; snapshot 2026-10-29T17:44:28Z. All 11 configured archives checked: 707 archive listings, 531 unique papers after versionless-ID deduplication. Ordering is inferred, not official or readership-based. Semantic Scholar yielded one usable record (2610.37383: citationCount 0, influentialCitationCount 0), so citation momentum was too sparse to drive ranking. The three leading papers were inspected in full-text arXiv HTML; direct official arXiv HTML/API retrieval substituted because the configured web extractor was unavailable.
